evidence_establishes: Counter-type adaptation studies in this project have found apparent lifts that shrink under adversarial checks (SF-APPA-067), are not replicable cross-game (SF-CHT-020), and suffer from selection/regression-to-the-mean artifacts (SF13).
Play-type identification from NBA data can be used to rank team efficiency (SF-APPM-001), but labeling complex defensive schemes is unreliable (SF-APPS-058).
Player-level analyses frequently have insufficient exposure (SF-APPA-066).
evidence_does_not_establish: No study has directly tested the claim that pull-up jumpers after a failed PNR provide a league-wide counter with lift >0 in ≥70% of units and median lift >2pp.
The historical evidence does not provide a validated definition of PNR failure or a method for isolating the causal effect of the counter.
It does not establish the expected base rate of pull-up sequences after PNR failure or the typical variance of the lift metric.
own_inferences: A naive comparison of pull-up efficiency after PNR failure vs other pull-ups will be confounded by regression to the mean (teams that just failed may have temporarily lower expected efficiency, making any subsequent positive outcome appear as a lift) and by defensive adjustments.
The 'unit' definition (team-season, team-game, opponent-season) will affect exposure; many units will have few qualifying sequences, raising multiple-testing and stability concerns.
The 2pp median threshold is tightly specified but the distributional requirement (≥70% positive) could be met spuriously if unit counts are small and lift estimates noisy.
uncertainties: The exact operational definition of a PNR failure (zero points, turnover, non-scoring possession) and whether 'lift' is measured as absolute PPP difference or relative to a baseline are not stated.
The reliability of play-type labels for PNR and PULL_UP in the graph database is unknown, though prior work (SF-APPM-001) suggests usable accuracy for common play types.
Whether the 70% threshold refers to independent units (e.g., 30 teams) or many small units (e.g., team-games) is ambiguous, impacting power and multiplicity.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical evidence shows that similar counter lift claims are prone to regression-to-the-mean artifacts (SF13) and that lifts shrink under adversarial checks (SF-APPA-067). These established risks directly undermine the proposed naive test. Without incorporating design elements to address RTM and exposure, the test is likely to produce an artifact, leading to the decision not to proceed.

blocking_constraints.text: The number of possessions in which a PNR failure is immediately followed by a pull-up attempt is likely small per unit (team-season or game), leading to unstable lift estimates.
Conditioning on PNR failure selects possessions where the offense underperformed, and any subsequent scoring improvement may be regression to the mean rather than a causal counter effect.
Play-type labels (PNR, PULL_UP) may have misclassification errors, diluting or biasing the measured lift.
Testing many units for lift >0 inflates the risk of false positives, especially with small per-unit sample sizes.
Defensive adjustments, game situation (shot clock, score margin), and personnel changes after a PNR failure could influence pull-up efficiency independently of any counter strategy.

prior_work.summary: No prior study directly assessed the PNR-fail to pull-up counter. Related work on counter strategies found artifacts and exposure limitations, and established that play-type mix can predict PPP, but did not validate the specific counter.

risks.text: Per-unit counts of PNR-fail-to-pull-up sequences are likely too low for reliable lift estimation and hypothesis testing.
Selecting on PNR failure introduces regression to the mean; any apparent lift may be statistical artifact.
Misclassification of play types (PNR, PULL_UP) can bias the measured lift.
The requirement that >=70% of units show positive lift creates a multiple-testing problem across many units.
Post-failure changes in defensive strategy, shot clock, and player personnel can confound the pull-up efficiency.
Pooling multiple seasons may introduce nonstationarity in league play-style or rule changes that affect counter effectiveness.

design.estimand: Causal effect on points per possession (PPP) of using a pull-up field-goal attempt vs. another play type immediately following a PNR possession that yielded zero points, aggregated to the team-season level.
design.sample: All regular-season and playoff possessions from 2022-23 through 2025-26 where the previous possession was a PNR resulting in zero points (non-scoring outcome: missed shot, turnover, end-of-possession non-shooting foul without free throws) and the current possession is either a pull-up field-goal attempt or an alternate play type. Exclude end-of-quarter heaves.
design.power: Require a minimum of 50 qualifying pull-up possessions per team-season; otherwise pool adjacent seasons for the same team to reach the threshold. With ~2-3 such sequences per game and 82-game seasons, about 200 per team-season, though not all will meet the threshold. A one-sample t-test per unit for lift >0 with 0.02 PPP effect, SD 0.8, n=50 has ~80% power at alpha 0.05. For the league-wide threshold test, a one-sided binomial test of proportion >=0.7 across ~100 units has >80% power to detect a true proportion 0.7 vs 0.5.
design.controls: Possession-level covariates: shot-clock remaining (categorical buckets), period, score differential, opponent defensive rating over the preceding season, and an indicator for whether the pull-up was assisted. Unit-level model with random intercepts for team and opponent.
design.falsification: Placebo test: replace the preceding PNR failure with a random non-PNR play that also scored zero points; the pull-up lift should disappear. Test whether the lift is symmetric by examining pull-ups after successful PNR (where no counter would be expected). Split the sample temporally (first two seasons vs. last two) to test stability.
design.multiplicity: Prespecify the single counter (PNR-fail to pull-up) as the primary test; no multiplicity adjustment needed. If multiple counter claims are examined, control the false discovery rate across them.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null of no counter if (a) the fraction of team-seasons with mean lift >0 is >=0.70 with 95% confidence lower bound above 0.70, and (b) the median team-season lift is >=0.02 PPP with the lower bound of a 95% bootstrap confidence interval above 0.02.
design.data_version: Graph database derived from NBA stats API play-by-play and matchups, with play-type labels validated against a holdout set (as in SF-APPA-063). Version: 2025-26 complete season snapshot.
